# Random Segfault or Double Free When Calculating the Frame Jacobian After Adding the Frame, How to Fix the Original Thread?

> **Current answer:** The original code first executes model.createData(), then model.addFrame(frame), and uses the old data to compute the Jacobian. A project member pointed out that the Data should not be modified after model.createData() is called; the original author confirmed this was their order. The handling is to complete model modifications such as addFrame() before creating the Data; when modifying the Model later, the Data should also be rebuilt. The original author confirmed the order was incorrect.

## Problem and symptoms

- Pinocchio calls getFrameJacobian randomly causes segmentation faults, bus errors, or double free; check which object's lifetime is the issue.
- Same script causes unstable segmentation faults, bus errors, corrupted double-linked list, or double free.

## Environment

- Pinocchio 2.6.19 (pip); Python 3.10.4; UR5 URDF; x86_64 Linux, Intel i7-8550U.

## Priority diagnostics

- Checking the order of model.createData() and model.addFrame(): the original example changed the Model's frame structure after Data was already created.

## Possible causes

- Project member confirmed that Pinocchio Data was created before Pinocchio Model.

## Attempts

- The project member suggested moving model.createData() after model.addFrame(frame); another contributor agreed with this diagnosis, and the original author confirmed the order was incorrect.

## Effective fixes

- Complete all Model structure modifications before calling model.createData(); if the Model is modified again, re-create the corresponding Data before running Jacobian/kinematic algorithms.

## Result

- Original author confirmed adding frames after initializing Data and accepted the correction. Issue was subsequently marked as completed.
